subject: physics
title: Specific heat capacity
apparatus: metal block; heater; insulation; thermometer/probe; joulemeter or ammeter/voltmeter; balance; stopwatch
dependentVariable: temperature change and calculated specific heat capacity
controlVariables: mass; insulation; heater power; starting temperature; contact
methodOverview: Measure block mass, insert heater and thermometer with good thermal contact, insulate, record initial temperature, supply measured electrical energy, record temperature over time and calculate c = E/(mΔT).
accuracyReliability: Use thermal paste, tight insulation, calibrated sensors, joulemeter/data logger and repeated readings; use gradient if appropriate.
safety: Heater/block become hot; switch off before handling; check leads and use low voltage.
scientificRationale: Insulation reduces energy loss; thermal paste reduces air gaps; electrical energy is estimated by E = VIt or joulemeter.
expectedPattern: Temperature rises approximately linearly at first; calculated c is often too high if energy losses are ignored.
dataGraphFocus: Plot temperature against energy or time; gradient links ΔT and E for fixed mass.
commonError: Energy heats the heater, thermometer and surroundings as well as the block.
improvement: Improve insulation, use thermal paste, account for heater heat capacity or extrapolate initial gradient.

subject: physics
title: Thermal insulation
apparatus: containers; hot water; lids; insulation materials; thermometer/probe; measuring cylinder; stopwatch
controlVariables: water volume; initial temperature; container; surface area; room conditions; time
methodOverview: Fill identical containers with equal hot-water volumes at the same starting temperature, apply different insulation, record temperature at fixed intervals and compare cooling rates.
accuracyReliability: Use lids, identical containers, temperature probes/data logging, simultaneous runs or controlled room conditions and repeats.
safety: Take care with hot water; dry spills; keep liquids away from electrical equipment.
scientificRationale: Equal starting conditions make insulation the only major difference; lid reduces convection/evaporation; trapped air lowers conduction.
expectedPattern: Better/thicker insulation gives a smaller temperature drop or shallower cooling curve, with diminishing benefit at large thickness.
dataGraphFocus: Plot temperature against time; compare initial gradients or temperature loss after equal time.
commonError: Different room draughts or exposed top areas alter cooling independently of wall insulation.
improvement: Use lids, draught shield, randomise positions, run simultaneously and repeat.

subject: physics
title: Resistance of circuits
apparatus: power supply; ammeter; voltmeter; switch; test wire; ruler; crocodile clips; resistors
controlVariables: wire material/thickness; temperature; supply; contact quality
methodOverview: Connect ammeter in series and voltmeter in parallel. Change wire length using a sliding contact, record V and I, calculate R = V/I; also compare resistor combinations in series and parallel.
accuracyReliability: Switch off between readings, use low current to limit heating, measure length between contacts, check zero/contact resistance and repeat.
safety: Use low voltage; wire may become hot; switch off before changing circuit.
scientificRationale: Longer wire gives more lattice interactions and larger resistance; heating changes resistance; series adds resistance while parallel provides more paths.
expectedPattern: Resistance is proportional to length for constant material, area and temperature; total series resistance rises, total parallel resistance falls.
dataGraphFocus: Plot resistance against length; expect a straight line through/near origin and interpret intercept.
commonError: Wire heating raises resistance and bends the graph away from direct proportionality.
improvement: Use lower current, brief readings, switch off between readings and allow cooling.

subject: physics
title: I–V characteristics
apparatus: DC supply; ammeter; voltmeter; variable resistor; fixed resistor; lamp; diode; switch
controlVariables: component; temperature control where required; circuit; reading intervals
methodOverview: Construct circuit with ammeter in series, voltmeter across component and variable resistor. Vary potential difference, record V and I in both directions where appropriate, and plot I against V.
accuracyReliability: Use small intervals, reverse supply safely, switch off to control heating, take repeat readings and plot correct axes.
safety: Use low voltage; lamp becomes hot; switch off before changing components/polarity.
scientificRationale: Variable resistor controls current; reversing supply reveals diode direction; lamp heating raises resistance.
expectedPattern: Ohmic resistor: straight line through origin at constant temperature; filament lamp: decreasing gradient; diode: negligible reverse current and forward threshold.
dataGraphFocus: Plot current on y-axis against potential difference on x-axis; gradient relates to conductance for an I–V graph.
commonError: Taking readings too slowly heats the resistor/lamp and changes resistance.
improvement: Use brief readings, low currents, allow cooling and data logging.

subject: physics
title: Density
apparatus: balance; ruler/calipers; displacement can; measuring cylinder; water; thread; regular/irregular solids
controlVariables: balance zero; reading technique; trapped air; water loss; temperature
methodOverview: Measure mass. For regular solids calculate volume from dimensions; for irregular solids measure displaced water volume. Calculate density = mass/volume with consistent units.
accuracyReliability: Zero balance, use calipers for small dimensions, read meniscus at eye level, fully submerge without trapped bubbles and repeat.
safety: Prevent spills; handle displacement cans/glassware and heavy objects carefully.
scientificRationale: Displacement volume equals submerged object volume; consistent units are essential; density is a material property for uniform samples.
expectedPattern: Objects of same material have similar density despite different size; floating depends on average density relative to fluid.
dataGraphFocus: Compare measured densities with reference values and uncertainty; identify anomalous volumes.
commonError: Water clinging to object or missing the measuring cylinder changes measured volume.
improvement: Collect all overflow, wait for dripping to stop before start, use a narrow graduated cylinder and repeat.

subject: physics
title: Force and extension
apparatus: spring; clamp stand; masses; ruler; pointer; safety goggles
controlVariables: same spring; starting length; loading increments; ruler position; no oscillation
methodOverview: Measure original spring length, add known loads in steps, allow settling, measure new length and calculate extension. Unload in steps to check return and plot force against extension.
accuracyReliability: Use a pointer and fixed ruler at eye level, small increments, repeat loading/unloading and stay below elastic limit.
safety: Secure stand with a heavy base; wear eye protection; catch falling masses; do not overload spring.
scientificRationale: Extension is change in length; settling prevents oscillation error; unloading tests elastic behaviour.
expectedPattern: Below limit of proportionality force is proportional to extension; beyond it graph curves; beyond elastic limit permanent deformation remains.
dataGraphFocus: Plot force on y-axis against extension on x-axis; gradient is spring constant k for F = ke.
commonError: Parallax and measuring total length instead of extension distort results.
improvement: Use a pointer, eye-level scale, calculate extension from initial length and repeat.

subject: physics
title: Acceleration
apparatus: trolley; ramp; light gates/motion sensor; data logger; metre ruler; masses; pulley; ticker timer
controlVariables: track angle/friction; trolley system; starting position; force/mass depending investigation
methodOverview: Set up trolley with motion sensor/light gates. Change resultant force while keeping total mass constant, or change mass while keeping force constant. Release without push, record acceleration and repeat.
accuracyReliability: Use electronic timing, long enough track, level/consistent track, low-friction pulley, fixed release and repeats.
safety: Secure track/pulley; use a stop block; keep feet clear of falling masses.
scientificRationale: Controlling mass isolates F effect; controlling force isolates m effect; release without push avoids extra force.
expectedPattern: For fixed mass, acceleration is proportional to resultant force; for fixed force, acceleration decreases as mass increases.
dataGraphFocus: Plot a against F for fixed m (straight line) or a against 1/m for fixed F; account for friction/intercept.
commonError: Ignoring mass of hanger/string or friction makes theoretical acceleration too high.
improvement: Include total moving mass, measure frictional force/intercept, align apparatus and repeat.

subject: physics
title: Waves
apparatus: ripple tank; signal generator; lamp; ruler; strobe; string; vibration generator
controlVariables: water depth; amplitude; measurement region; string length/tension as appropriate
methodOverview: Generate steady waves. Measure distance across several wavelengths and divide; measure frequency from generator; calculate v = fλ. Repeat for different conditions while controlling the medium.
accuracyReliability: Measure many wavelengths, use strobe/frozen image, avoid edge reflections, repeat and use consistent water depth.
safety: Keep water away from electrical equipment; use low-voltage apparatus; wipe spills.
scientificRationale: Several wavelengths reduce percentage uncertainty; fixed medium allows effect of frequency to be tested; wave speed depends on medium.
expectedPattern: In the same medium wave speed is approximately constant, so increasing frequency decreases wavelength.
dataGraphFocus: Plot wavelength against 1/f or calculate v for repeats; identify reflected/interfering waves.
commonError: Counting crests near tank edges includes reflected waves.
improvement: Measure in central region, use absorbers, strobe image and several wavelengths.

subject: physics
title: Reflection and refraction of light
apparatus: ray box/laser; slit; mirror; glass block; paper; ruler; protractor
dependentVariable: angle of reflection/refraction and ray path
controlVariables: same block; ray colour; point of incidence; measurement method
methodOverview: Trace block/mirror, draw normal, direct a narrow ray at measured incidence angles, mark ray positions, remove apparatus, join points and measure angles from the normal.
accuracyReliability: Use widely spaced marks, thin beam, sharp pencil, large angles, repeat and avoid moving block.
safety: Do not look into laser/ray box; keep beam below eye level; glass may have sharp edges.
scientificRationale: Angles are measured from normal; marking points then removing block avoids measuring through it; refraction occurs because wave speed changes.
expectedPattern: Angle of reflection equals incidence; ray bends toward normal entering optically denser medium and away leaving.
dataGraphFocus: Plot reflected/refracted angle against incidence; assess equality and uncertainty.
commonError: Thick pencil lines and measuring from surface instead of normal cause systematic error.
improvement: Use sharp pencil/thin beam, larger diagram, repeat from both sides and measure from normal.

subject: physics
title: Infrared radiation and absorption
apparatus: Leslie cube or identical surfaces; hot water; infrared detector; ruler; thermometer
controlVariables: temperature; area; distance/angle; material; room background; time
methodOverview: Heat surfaces to the same temperature, place IR detector at fixed distance and angle, record intensity for different finishes; or compare cooling of identical containers with different surfaces.
accuracyReliability: Equalise temperature, fixed geometry, background correction, repeat and avoid touching surfaces.
safety: Hot water/surfaces can burn; secure containers; do not overfill.
scientificRationale: Surface finish affects emission/absorption; fixed temperature and geometry isolate emissivity; detector response depends on distance.
expectedPattern: Matt black is best emitter and absorber; shiny light surfaces are poor emitters/absorbers and good reflectors.
dataGraphFocus: Compare mean detector readings or cooling curves; control temperature because emission strongly depends on it.
commonError: Surfaces cool at different rates, so later readings are taken at unequal temperatures.
improvement: Measure rapidly at same temperature, reheat/equilibrate between readings, use simultaneous sensors and repeat.
